content.title: Oscars 2026 recap: ‘One Battle After Another’ wins best picture after big night
content.text: 1 minIt was a showdown between “Sinners” and “One Battle After Another” at the 2026 Oscars Sunday night, but in the end it was Paul Thomas Anderson’s thriller about left-wing ex-revolutionaries that won best picture. The hotly contested best actor race saw Michael B. Jordan emerge victorious for “Sinners,” while Jessie Buckley won best actress for “Hamnet.” Key updatesFollow MoviesLive coverage contributors 810:55 p.m. EDTReturn to menu“Sinners” may have set the record for the most nominations in Oscars history (16) and relished an electrifying win for best ensemble at the Actor Awards earlier this month, setting the stage for a potential best picture upset Sunday. But “One Battle After Another” turned out to be an awards season front-runner that never fell out of pole position. Every major precursor with a best picture prize — the BAFTAs, Producers Guild of America Awards, Golden Globes and Critics Choice Awards — anointed Paul Thomas Anderson’s sprawling tale of political revolution. And “One Battle” walked away with a ceremony-high six Oscars: picture, director, adapted screenplay, supporting actor, film editing and casting.10:48 p.m. EDTReturn to menuStar Teyana Taylor rushed the stage jubilantly when “One Battle After Another” won best picture. Director Paul Thomas Anderson acknowledged his fellow nominees, saying “There is no best, there is just what the mood is that day.” He also said he “really blew it when I won a best director award and I forgot to thank my cast,” acknowledging the assembled cast of the film behind him, and singling out “My American girl, Chase” Infiniti. He concluded: “Let’s have a martini, this is pretty amazing.”10:38 p.m. EDTReturn to menuI can say with certainty: Jessie Buckley deserved to win..... But so did everyone else!Can we spread this best actress category over the next five years, please?10:36 p.m. EDTReturn to menuThere was no upset in the one acting category that seemed sewn up entering the night: Jessie Buckley won best actress for her wrenching portrayal of William Shakespeare’s grieving wife, Agnes, in “Hamnet.” The victory concluded Buckley’s awards season steamrolling, which also included wins at the Actor Awards, BAFTAs, Critics Choice Awards and Golden Globes. “It’s Mother’s Day in the U.K. today,” Buckley said. “So I would like to dedicate this to the beautiful chaos of a mother’s heart.”10:36 p.m. EDT‘One Battle After Another’ won best picture10:32 p.m. EDTReturn to menuWhat a night for Michael B. Jordan — his first ever Oscar nomination and his first big win, all at once. Two big firsts for the “Sinners” actor, who played twin gangsters in the supernatural thriller, in one of the most contentious races of the year.“I stand here because of the people that came before me,” Jordan said, naming prominent Black actors whose footsteps he followed to the podium. “Those greats, amongst my ancestors, amongst my guys. Thank you, everybody in this room, and everyone at home, for supporting me over my career.”Last year’s best actor winner, Adrian Brody, presented the award after a bit about his uber-long 2025 speech — the longest in Oscar history, at nearly six minutes. This was a tight race, but it didn’t start off that way. Timothée Chalamet was initially favored to win for his exhausting titular narcissist in “Marty Supreme” until his campaign style drew criticism from industry pros and voters (and, of course, opera and ballet performers).10:30 p.m. EDTJessie Buckley won best actress in a leading role for ‘Hamnet’10:23 p.m. EDTReturn to menuPaul Thomas Anderson, who won his first Oscar earlier tonight for best adapted screenplay, also snagged best director for “One Battle After Another,” a thriller about left-wing ex-revolutionaries that doubles as a stoner comedy and a coming-of-age film. He mentioned his former assistant director Adam Somner, who died in 2024. Joking his more than two decades of non-winning nominations, Anderson added: “You make a guy work hard for one of these.”10:22 p.m. EDTReturn to menuPopular opinion: Adrien Brody is annoying.Unpopular opinion: Adrien Broday’s brooch is not annoying!10:21 p.m. EDTMichael B. Jordan won best actor in a leading role for ‘Sinners’10:18 p.m. EDTReturn to menuNo surprise here — it’s their moment. “Golden” from “KPop Demon Hunters” won best song, and EJAE accepted her first Oscar after a tremendous rise to fame. The song, she said, was about resilience.“Growing up people made fun of me liking K-pop but now everyone’s singing our song, and all the Korean lyrics, and I’m so proud,” she said.10:17 p.m. EDTPaul Thomas Anderson won best director for ‘One Battle After Another’10:11 p.m. EDTReturn to menuIn one of the night’s more competitive categories, Norway’s “Sentimental Value" topped Brazil’s “The Secret Agent” for the international feature prize. Evoking James Baldwin, director Joachim Trier concluded his speech with a call to action. “All adults are responsible for all children,” he said. “And let’s not vote for politicians who don’t take this seriously.”The segment got off to a political start when presenter Javier Bardem declared, “No to war, and free Palestine.”10:11 p.m. EDT‘Golden’ from ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ won best original song10:10 p.m. EDTReturn to menu“Sentimental Value,” which won best international feature, was far and away the least interesting nominee. It’s impossible to forget the horrifying EDM buzz of “Sirât” or the simmering rage of “It Was Just an Accident” from Iranian auteur Jafar Panahi. Plus, “The Secret Agent” has Wagner Moura in his best performance yet. A disappointing pick.10:07 p.m. EDTReturn to menuThirteen-and-under crowd, rejoice. It’s “GOLDEN” TIME! The original song nominee from “KPop Demon Hunters” has been inescapable since its release, especially for parents of the Gen Alpha crowd. But who, with a beating heart of any age, could resist those belted high notes from the HUNTR/X vocalists?EJAE, Audrey Nuna and Rei Ami delivered a high-energy live version in front of an audience waving the sort of light sticks more often found at k-pop concerts than award shows. They looked dashing in crisp complimentary white getups, and we clocked those gold accents.10:05 p.m. EDT‘Sentimental Value’ won best international feature film10:01 p.m. EDTReturn to menuI have so much secondhand anxiety about the “KPop Demon Hunters” sequel. The first time was a fluke. This time there will be so much pressure!And I’m not sure if you can improve on the first. But I’m pretty sure you can’t improve on “Golden.”10:00 p.m. EDTReturn to menuAutumn Durald Arkapaw is the first woman to win best cinematography, for her warm, evocative photography that rooted “Sinners” in the Mississippi Delta of 1932. (Only three other women have been nominated in the category, and Arkapaw was the first woman of color.) After thanking director Ryan Coogler, she called for all of the women in the room to stand with her and hailed Rachel Morrison, who was the first woman to be nominated for best cinematography in 2017. “I have felt so much love from all of the women on this whole campaign,” Arkapaw said.9:56 p.m. EDTReturn to menuAlso a great night for dapper women!A lovely suit and tie on Autumn Durald Arkapaw (first woman to win an Oscar for cinematography)! And great tuxes on Tig Notaro, Fortune Feimster and Brandi Carlile!9:55 p.m. EDTReturn to menuMan oh man, Jessie Buckley’s Chanel dress really looks great in that front row.Between her and Teyana and Paris Fashion Week: Chanel is baaaack, baby!9:53 p.m. EDTReturn to menuThe Oscar for film editing — which presenter Bill Pullman called “an invisible art form” — went to Andy Jurgensen for “One Battle After Another.”He dedicated the award — his first Oscar win and nomination — to his aunt, a longtime archivist for the academy, and thanked director Paul Thomas Anderson for “taking me on this journey.”“I want to give a shout-out to all of my friends who are at a bar watching me,” Jurgensen said. “You can order some shots now.”9:50 p.m. EDT‘Sinners’ won best cinematography9:48 p.m. EDT‘One Battle After Another’ won best film editing9:46 p.m. EDTReturn to menuOkay, I’m still not over Anna Wintour.Decent comic timing with the shades and the shade.But … this look? She famously hates the color black!Well, I unfamously hate this Dior look.9:45 p.m. EDTReturn to menuThis is the third best score trophy for Ludwig Göransson, who also won for “Oppenheimer” and “Black Panther,” another Ryan Coogler film. But it’s the Swedish composer’s first time orchestrating a film steeped in the rich textures of blues music, as he did with “Sinners.”“I was about seven years old, a little boy, when [my father] put a guitar in my arms and it became everything to me,” he said. “It was the guitar that opened up a lot of work for me. It was the guitar that brought me over to the States, and it was the guitar that eventually led me to one of the greatest storytellers of our times, Ryan Coogler.”9:43 p.m. EDTReturn to menuThe auto-racing blockbuster “F1” just earned its first win of the night, claiming the prize for sound. Gwendolyn Yates Whittle, one of the recipients, used her speech to tout the cinematic experience. “Go see the blockbusters,” Whittle said. “Go see the independents. Be inspired. Go with a friend. Get a fresh point of view.”9:41 p.m. EDTReturn to menu“Bridesmaids” is somehow 15 years old. To celebrate, the academy asked the leading ladies (Melissa McCarthy, Ellie Kemper, Maya Rudolph, Kristen Wiig and Rose Byrne) to introduce best original score. Each of them read notes handed to them before they got onstage. The best one? The kid from “Hamnet” supposedly wrote that he’s tired and wants to go home. “This show is very long and there’s no pizza,” he reportedly wrote to Kemper.9:36 p.m. EDT‘F1’ won best sound9:33 p.m. EDTReturn to menuBaby Yoda — whose government name is Grogu but who will always be called Baby Yoda by the fans — is the weirdest and best cameo of this Oscars broadcast so far. The puppet featured in a bit where Sigourney Weaver yelled at Kate Hudson for flirting with him (“Get away from him, you b----,” she said), and host Conan O’Brien poked fun at the puppet for not being able to clap — instant reaction GIF fodder. “The Mandalorian and Grogu” comes out later this year.9:32 p.m. EDT‘Sinners’ won best original score9:30 p.m. EDTReturn to menuJimmy Kimmel, whose talk show was suspended by ABC in September after comments about the death of commentator Charlie Kirk, presented the Oscar for best documentary short — with a jab about “Melania,” the first lady’s biographical documentary.But politics became more personal when “All the Empty Rooms,” which memorialized the vacant bedrooms of four children lost to school shootings, won the award.“Gun violence is now the number one cause of death in kids and teens,” said the mother of a 9-year-old killed in her elementary school. “We believe if the world would see their empty bedrooms, it would be a different America.”9:29 p.m. EDTReturn to menuThe documentary feature prize went to “Mr. Nobody Against Putin,” which follows a Russian schoolteacher as he pushes back against the pro-war messaging of Vladimir Putin’s government. “In the name of our future and in the name of all our children, stop all of these wars now,” said Pavel Talankin, the film’s star and co-director, via an interpreter.9:25 p.m. EDTReturn to menuJimmy Kimmel didn’t mention President Trump by name when he was presenting best documentary feature, but it was easy to guess who he was referencing with this quip: “Oh man, is he gonna be mad his wife wasn’t nominated for this.”9:20 p.m. EDT‘Mr. Nobody Against Putin’ won best documentary feature film9:17 p.m. EDT‘All the Empty Rooms’ won best documentary short film9:14 p.m. EDTReturn to menuIt’s a year of pastoral environments and detailed period pieces on screen. But the academy was swayed by the gothic sci-fi world constructed in “Frankenstein,” giving Tamara Deverell and Shane Vieau the nod for best production design. Deverell had a speech ready on her iPhone and concluded by thanking “Frankenstein” novelist Mary Shelley.9:08 p.m. EDT‘Avatar: Fire and Ash’ won best visual effects9:06 p.m. EDTReturn to menuBarbra Streisand delivered a tribute to Robert Redford, who died in September at 89, fondly recalling filming “The Way We Were.” She called him an “intellectual cowboy” who had a real backbone and spoke up to protect what he believed in, from art to the environment. She talked about how he would tease her and call her “Babs,” to which she would reply, “Bob, do I look like a Babs?!” But she said that’s how she signed the last note she wrote to him. Then Streisand sang a few lines of “The Way We Were,” and we’re just guessing that more than a few people in the audience were weeping.9:06 p.m. EDT‘Frankenstein’ won best production design9:01 p.m. EDTReturn to menuThe in memoriam segment continued with Rachel McAdams honoring a slew of iconic actresses, including Claudia Cardinale, Diane Ladd and Catherine O’Hara. McAdams saved her most moving comments for her “Family Stone” co-star Diane Keaton, who died in October at 79. “Believe me when I say there isn’t an actress of my generation who wasn’t inspired by and enthralled with her absolute singularity,” McAdams said.8:59 p.m. EDTReturn to menu“When Harry Met Sally” star Billy Crystal delivered a touching tribute speech to director Rob Reiner and photographer Michele Reiner, who were found dead in their Los Angeles home in December. (Their middle son Nick Reiner was charged with murder in their deaths.) Crystal met Reiner, he said, playing his best friend on an episode of “All in the Family.”“My friend Rob’s movies will last a lifetime because they were about what makes us laugh and cry and what we aspired to be, far better in his eyes, far kinder, or funnier or far more human,” he said.Over a dozen actors who starred in Reiner’s enduring films — “Spinal Tap,” “The Princess Bride,” “Stand By Me” — stood side-by-side along the stage, grasped hands and turned to watch a montage of his movie’s finest moments.8:44 p.m. EDTReturn to menuAfter he won best original screenplay for “Sinners,” Ryan Coogler received the night’s rowdiest standing ovation so far. He invited the film’s cast and crew to share in the victory by standing up. “Y’all are winners in my book,” Coogler said. It’s the horror-musical’s first award tonight — but judging by the applause, don’t count it out for best picture.8:40 p.m. EDTReturn to menuPaul Thomas Anderson took the stage to big applause from the crowd after he won for best adapted screenplay — his first Oscar after 14 nominations. (He could still win two more tonight, for best director and best picture.) He thanked Thomas Pynchon, who wrote the novel “Vineland” that inspired “One Battle After Another,” as well as his family and partner, Maya Rudolph. He revealed that he wrote the film, set in a very bleak world, to his kids as an apology for the “housekeeping mess” that his generation is leaving behind. But he said he’s hopeful that they are the generation that will restore “common sense and decency.”8:37 p.m. EDT‘Sinners’ won best writing for an original screenplay8:33 p.m. EDT‘One Battle After Another’ won best writing for an adapted screenplay8:32 p.m. EDTReturn to menuIt’s a tie! But this surprising outcome for best short film is not completely unprecedented — Oscars ties have occurred before, most recently in 2013, when “Skyfall” and “Zero Dark Thirty” shared the award for best sound editing. In 1969, Barbra Streisand and Katharine Hepburn tied for best actress (Streisand won for her screen debut in “Funny Girl,” while Hepburn won for “The Lion in Winter”).The tie has provided plenty of fodder for jokes. “You just ruined 22 million Oscar pools,” said host Conan O’Brien.8:30 p.m. EDTReturn to menuSean Penn just became the eighth person in Oscars history with three acting wins, claiming the supporting actor prize for his squirmy performance in “One Battle After Another.” (He previously won for “Mystic River” and “Milk.”) But after skipping his victories at the BAFTAs and Actor Awards, Penn was again a no-show. “Sean Penn couldn’t be here this evening — or didn’t want to,” quipped the presenter, last year’s winner Kieran Culkin.8:24 p.m. EDTReturn to menuFor just the seventh time in Academy Awards history, two nominees tied for an Oscar. “The Singers,” an adaptation of Turgenev’s 1850s Russian novel set in contemporary America, and “Two People Exchanging Saliva,” about a society where kissing is punishable by death, both took home an award.“Ironic that the short film Oscar is going to take twice as long,” said presenter Kumail Nanjiani.8:23 p.m. EDTSean Penn won best actor in a supporting role for ‘One Battle After Another’8:18 p.m. EDTIn a tie, ‘The Singers’ and ‘Two People Exchanging Saliva’ won best live action short film8:14 p.m. EDTReturn to menuThe first-ever best casting award went to Cassandra Kulukundis, who assembled the sprawling troupe in “One Battle After Another.” She dedicated her award to the casting directors who weren’t acknowledged in the past, before thanking the film’s director, whom she’s worked alongside since the ’90s. “When Paul Thomas Anderson calls you,” Kulukundis said, “you enter the PTA protection program.”8:05 p.m. EDT‘One Battle After Another’ won best casting8:02 p.m. EDTReturn to menuSeconds after “Frankenstein” won for best costume design, the hair and makeup team followed to pick up the movie’s second trophy. Mike Hill, alongside his colleagues Jordan Samuel and Cliona Furey, thanked the cast — especially Jacob Elordi, who sat for 400 hours in the makeup chair during filming — and director/writer/producer Guillermo del Toro. Hill thanked him for “allowing us to help your dream project become our dream project.”7:59 p.m. EDTReturn to menuThe costume design prize — presented by “The Devil Wears Prada 2” star Anne Hathaway (!) and Condé Nast executive Anna Wintour (!!!) — went to “Frankenstein’s” Kate Hawley. “All of our nominations are your nominations,” Hawley said to director Guillermo del Toro. “We share this with you.” This figures to be one of several below-the-line wins for “Frankenstein,” which is also favored to triumph for production design and makeup and hairstyling.7:55 p.m. EDT‘Frankenstein’ won best makeup and hairstyling7:52 p.m. EDTReturn to menuOne of the most goosebump-inducing moments of “Sinners” falls mid-performance at a jukebox joint, when Miles Caton’s character sings the original acoustic blues song “I Lied to You.” Then an electric guitar riff kicks in, and the dance scene becomes a montage of Black artistic excellence through the ages, from rock to funk to rap. That moment proved no less enthralling — or important — on stage, where the cast played the track live, joined by, among others, Misty Copeland, Brittany Howard, Shaboozey and Alice Smith.7:52 p.m. EDT‘Frankenstein’ won best costume design7:44 p.m. EDTReturn to menuWhile accepting the award for best animated short for “The Girl Who Cried Pearls,” Chris Lavis joked about how people think it takes patience to make a puppet film over the course of five years. “It actually takes patience to live with someone who takes five years to make a puppet film,” Lavis said, laughing, before thanking his family.7:41 p.m. EDTReturn to menu“KPop Demon Hunters” took over pop culture last year, so it wasn’t a huge shock to see it win the trophy for animated feature — and it led to an emotional speech by the filmmakers.“Thank you to the academy and to all the fans who got us here. And for those of you who look like me, I’m so sorry that it took us so long to see us in a movie like this,” said co-director and screenwriter Maggie Kang. “But it is here, and that means that the next generations don’t have to go long. This is for Korea and for Koreans everywhere.” Chris Appelhans urged young filmmakers and artists to tell their stories, because these type of stories have the power to connect cultures: “I promise you, the world is waiting.”7:37 p.m. EDT‘The Girl Who Cried Pearls’ won best animated short film7:33 p.m. EDT‘KPop Demon Hunters’ won best animated feature film7:28 p.m. EDTReturn to menuConan O’Brien’s opening song at last year’s Oscars — “I Won’t Waste Time,” a riff on lengthy speeches — was a hard act to follow, but after a fiery opening monologue, the host delivered a regal tune about accepting a faux award for “Best Achievement.” With little of the humble gratitude that many winners espouse in their acceptances, O’Brien had himself draped with a red cape and donned a crown, while Josh Groban sang an operatic “Hallelujah” and a falcon delivered his Oscar atop his throne.7:28 p.m. EDTReturn to menuThe first award of the night came in one of the most unpredictable categories: supporting actress, where “Weapons” scene stealer Amy Madigan triumphed for her deliciously unhinged performance as the diabolical Aunt Gladys. This was Madigan’s second nomination — 40 years after she got her first nod for “Twice in a Lifetime.” “What’s different about this time?” Madigan asked. “What’s different is I got this little gold guy.”7:22 p.m. EDTAmy Madigan won best actress in a supporting role for ‘Weapons’7:20 p.m. EDTReturn to menuOnce Conan O’Brien took the stage, he joked about some of the lesser-known categories. But before he got a chance to share his punch line, the audience drowned him out with applause. It eventually died down and he shared a nickname for the documentary shorts category. “As I like to call them: Lil Sads,” O’Brien said.7:07 p.m. EDTReturn to menuThe ceremony kicks off with host Conan O’Brien doing a classic Oscars opening parody bit, in classic Conan style. He gets a makeover where he looks suspiciously like Amy Madigan’s character in “Weapons” (the makeup artist didn’t really even have to add that much makeup, she admits, and the wig isn’t that much of a stretch) and then is chased by a terrifying horde of children. He stops to play ping-pong, briefly appears in “KPop Demon Hunters,” shows up in the “Sinners” juke joint and then has the kids chase him up on to the Oscars stage.7:06 p.m. EDTReturn to menuIt’s so, so, so hard not to make a “Florals? For spring? Groundbreaking” joke about Anne Hathaway’s (honestly lovely) dress, especially because she is here to promote the upcoming “The Devil Wears Prada 2.”6:59 p.m. EDTReturn to menuPoints for taking a risk, but Alana Haim, who starred in “One Battle After Another,” is wearing a dress that drapes very strangely in the front.6:59 p.m. EDTReturn to menuPedro Pascal, bespectacled and shirt-sleeved in Chanel.No jacket. Guess he’s revealing more of himself these days.6:56 p.m. EDTThe dramatic transformation Ethan Hawke underwent for ‘Blue Moon’ Return to menuBefore Rodgers and Hammerstein, there was Rodgers and Hart.This is an excerpt from a full story.6:56 p.m. EDTReturn to menuOscars minimalism done well: Kirsten Dunst wears squared-off Celine, in cascading layers. Her husband, Jesse Plemons, is in the best picture-nominated “Bugonia.”6:55 p.m. EDTReturn to menuEthan Hawke, nominated for best actor in “Blue Moon,” in a three-piece suit by Prada.Between him and Kumail Nanjiani, I’m ... not sold on gray shirts.But somehow feeling good about long jackets? And magicians?6:49 p.m. EDTReturn to menuTimothée Chalamet in white-on-white-on-white Givenchy by Sarah Burton.A purification ritual of atonement for his shade to opera and ballet?6:49 p.m. EDTReturn to menuA night of lovely couples in less-than-lovely looks. Pobody’s nerfect!Spike Lee and Tonya Lewis, Kumail Nanjiani and Emily V. Gordon, Laurie Feig and Paul Feig.6:48 p.m. EDTReturn to menuKate Hudson, nominated for best actress for “Song Sung Blue,” is looking very mermaidy in this jade peplum Giorgio Armani Privé gown.6:46 p.m. EDTReturn to menuFitting that Teyana Taylor — one of Hollywood’s most electric new talents — would be wearing Chanel designed by Matthieu Blazy, one of fashion’s most electric new creative directors.It takes a lot of work to make something look this effortless. That refers to both the gown and Taylor, who is nominated for best supporting actress for her role in “One Battle After Another.”6:44 p.m. EDTReturn to menuOne fashion statement we’ve seen through awards season: Some stars wearing pins and carrying purses showing their disapproval of ICE. Glennon Doyle had a beaded clutch reading “F--k ICE.” And Malgosia Turzanska (nominated for costume design for “Hamnet”) and songwriter Sara Bareilles (an executive producer of nominated documentary “Come See Me in the Good Light”) are wearing “ICE OUT” pins.6:41 p.m. EDTReturn to menuPerfect fit. Whimsical cap sleeves. Daring backless cut. Sleek, long, confident lines.Hard to get much better than Emma Stone, nominated tonight for best actress in “Bugonia,” in Louis Vuitton.6:38 p.m. EDTReturn to menuLove seeing Shaboozey in Campillo, a label that has been throwing some of the more interesting runway shows at New York Fashion Week.And I love the pearl earrings, echoed in the string peeking out from the bottom of his jacket. Soft and strong!6:29 p.m. EDTReturn to menuInga Ibsdotter Lilleaas — nominated for best supporting actress for “Sentimental Value” — presents a novel take on the classic Oscars black-and-white column gown. Her custom Loewe gown is topped with a wave of wild beads — a wonderfully strange shape, sort of like a sea anemone. She paired it with diamond earrings that dangle from above her lobes.6:25 p.m. EDTReturn to menuUGH I just saw the finger details on Audrey Nuna.It’s like my wildest fantasy version of when I would put paper clips on my fingers to pretend I had long nails. LIVING THE DREAM, NUNA!!6:22 p.m. EDTReturn to menuElle Fanning, nominated for best supporting actress in “Sentimental Value,” is wearing Givenchy by Sarah Burton and a vintage necklace from 1903.She looks absolutely angelic, but it’s giving more bridal than bombshell, tbh.6:20 p.m. EDTReturn to menuSee what I mean about how good you look the year after you win an Oscar? Look how chill he looks in this brown and black suit? And clock the friendship beads he’s carrying. When he won for “A Real Pain” last year, he said he wanted a fourth kid.Tonight he’s serving BDE. That’s “boastful dad energy,” obviously.6:13 p.m. EDTReturn to menuDemi Moore’s feathered column — black and emerald green, like a goth peacock — is custom Gucci. Moore was a best actress nominee last year for “The Substance.”6:10 p.m. EDTReturn to menuI love the energy of someone who won an Oscar last year.Zoe Saldaña looks so relaxed, and so sure of herself, in this lacy satin-y spaghetti-strapped slip dress.I wish the necklace matched the ease of this lingerie-adjacent look, but whatever. It’s the Oscars. Sparkle!6:06 p.m. EDTReturn to menuBest supporting actress nominee Wunmi Mosaku (“Sinners”) in a cold shoulder glittering green maxi. And a baby bump. Elegance! Celebration!(And if you’re looking for a deep dive on the cold shoulder, check out this wonderful piece by Avery Trufelman.)5:59 p.m. EDTReturn to menuJerskin Fendrix is nominated for best original score for “Bugonia.”In this photo, he and Annie Hamilton are really giving too-cool-for-school, “Yeah, I guess we’re technically ‘at the Oscars,’” but somehow it works? Can I sit with them?5:59 p.m. EDTReturn to menuJessie Buckley — nominated for “Hamnet” and starring in newly released “The Bride!” — is favored to win best actress tonight, and this sure is a winning Chanel dress. Pink and red — such an optimistic color combo! — structured on top and flowy on the bottom, and her lipstick is the most precisely matching shade of red. An immediate contender for best dressed.5:50 p.m. EDTReturn to menuOdessa A’zion continues her uninterrupted streak of cool-girl curls on the red carpet. A’zion, who starred in “Marty Supreme,” seems to love a plunging neckline with billowy sleeves — this is a silhouette we’ve seen on her before. Love the off-center lariat necklace.5:48 p.m. EDTReturn to menu“KPop Demon Hunters” star Audrey Nuna’s awards season looks have been consistently brazen but inconsistently good.Her Thom Browne Oscars dress? WONDERFUL! Love the moire high-volume skirt, love the severe yet glittery jacket with its dithering strips of gold into black. She’s not nominated tonight — she doesn’t have a songwriting credit on “Golden,” which she’ll perform — but she may have already won.5:41 p.m. EDTReturn to menuWe all knew she was gonna be, gonna be golden: Here’s “KPop Demon Hunters” voice Ejae, in a gold column gown. The fringe keeps it from being too basic.5:38 p.m. EDTReturn to menuWhat is Diane Warren wearing?WHATEVER SHE WANTS. This is her 17th Oscar nomination for best song (this time for “Dear Me” from the documentary “Diane Warren: Relentless”).And no wins (so far)! From the woman who wrote “How Do I Live”???!
